comment: The single-cell T-pose reference guide, in the same normalised cell space the sheet guides use: x and y run 0..1 across one cell with y pointing down. It is drawn by spritesynth.render_guide through TPOSE_GEOMETRY -- one 1024px cell, deliberately outside the GEOMETRY registry, because a T-pose reference is not a sprite sheet and tests/test_sprite_geometry_agreement.py owns the claim that GEOMETRY, SHEET_TYPES and inker's SHEET_KINDS name the same set. The arms are horizontal and the legs are straight because this guide exists to make reconstruction and the bbox-proportional fit_template predictable, not to make an attractive illustration: limb separation and a wide, unambiguous silhouette are what TRELLIS needs from a single view. Feet at y 0.92 leave the headroom a hat or a crest needs without the figure ever touching the frame. This is DATA: the pose is iterable without touching any code.
